summary.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It is simplified from 國: the inner 或 in 國 is replaced by 玉 in 国. In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory and 或 supplies a sound cue; 玉 is not the historical sound element.

formation.text: The traditional graph 國 is phonosemantic: 囗 contributes boundary or territory meaning, while 或 supplies a sound cue. The curated Western Zhou bronze-style illustration shows the enclosed arrangement as a modern redraw, not an artifact image. 国 retains the enclosure but has 玉 in place of 或; the evidence does not explain why 玉 was chosen.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. Warring States forms are also reported with 匚 or 𠃊 in this boundary-marker role. This component belongs to 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the phonetic element; its original depicted referent is not established. It is replaced by 玉 in 国, so 或 is not a component of the current graph.

sound_limitation.text: The cited reconstructions show a sound relationship but do not establish 或’s original depicted referent. Modern readings alone do not prove its role in 國.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstructions, 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ are similar, with an initial consonant contrast. These are reconstructions, not direct records of ancient speech.

components.text: 玉 is the visible inner element in 国 and occupies the position of 或 in 國. This is a graphic replacement; the evidence does not explain why 玉 was chosen.

history.text: The curated illustration is a modern redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-script-style form: an angular inner element sits within an enclosure. It illustrates the reported structure of 國, not a directly inspected artifact or a proven sequence of graphic stages.

國 with 囗 is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions for “country/state.” Warring States forms may vary the boundary marker; later bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts also attest 國 with this meaning. These examples document usage without establishing a sequence of graphic stages or later meanings.

A Han-dynasty dictionary account analyzes 國 as 囗 plus 或 and glosses it as 邦. The proposed reading of 或 as “country” in the He zun inscription is disputed; another interpretation takes it as 域, “territory.”
国 is reported as simplified from 國 with 或 replaced by 玉, and as the Japanese shinjitai corresponding to 國. The exact path and date of this graphic change are not established by the cited evidence.

uncertainties.text: The secure earliest attestation of the spoken word meaning “country/state” remains unsettled: the proposed He zun reading of 或 as 國 is disputed, and the cited research does not include a complete inscription survey.
The evidence does not establish a dated semantic path from boundary or territory to polity, or the chronology of later senses such as “nation-state.”
The evidence reports the graphic replacement 或 → 玉 but does not establish its precise historical pathway or why 玉 was selected.

senses.period: Western Zhou inscriptions reported; exact earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions are reported to use 國 for “country/state.” This supports the sense in that period, while the disputed He zun reading of 或 leaves the word’s earliest attestation unsettled.
The character is currently used for “nation” and “country.” The evidence does not date how this range developed from the older country/state sense.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a dated semantic transition from territory or state to the current range “nation, country, nation-state.”

overview.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It comes from 國, where 或 sits inside a boundary marker; in 国, 玉 occupies that inner position. In 國, 或 provides a sound cue, not 玉.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. It belongs to the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the sound element, though its original pictured referent is unsettled. 国 has 玉 in its place.
玉 is the visible inner form in 国, replacing 或 from 國; the reason for this graphic choice is not established.

takeaway.text: The sound element in 國 is 或; 玉 in 国 is a later graphic replacement.

relationships.text: 囗 marks the boundary or territory in 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
